batches.message: docs(invoice-review): teach complete amount fields and immutable publication [AI-01 AI-02]

replacements.new: The session extracts invoice 17, repeats it, quarantines invoice 18's unreadable total, and reads the saved result. Compare the repeated result's artifact key and source hash. The tests also cover malformed numeric suffixes and interrupted/concurrent object publication. The fixture uses the same source parser; separate tests inject model output directly so a shared parser mistake cannot be hidden by fixture agreement.

Trace the two independent decisions:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Source["Complete source field"] --> Parse["Application grammar"]
  Parse --> Compare["Evidence and cents agree?"]
  Model["Model JSON"] --> Compare
  Compare -->|no| Review["REVIEW_REQUIRED"]
  Compare -->|yes| Accept["ACCEPTED"]
  Review --> Object["Publish complete immutable object"]
  Accept --> Object
  Object --> Pointer["Conditionally commit registry pointer"]
```

T

4. **Validate the complete field.** The application parser in `invoice_fields.py` checks the source independently of model output. Require USD, integer cents (not a boolean), and exact agreement with the parsed evidence and amount. Finding a valid-looking substring inside a malformed number is not enough.
5. **Publish bytes before their pointer.** On AWS, write the content-derived S3 object, then conditionally publish its pointer in DynamoDB. Locally, write and sync a same-directory temporary file, publish without replacing an existing object, and sync the directory before committing the SQLite pointer. Repeated publication verifies existing bytes; it never opens the committed file for truncation. A crash can leave an orphan, not permission to replace the winning result.

| Numeric prefix trap | `TOTAL USD 12.345`, `12.34e2`, or `12.34.99` | `REVIEW_REQUIRED`; never accept the `12.34` prefix |
|

The reference accepts exactly one standalone `TOTAL` field: `TOTAL USD 12.34`.
Use 1–6 ASCII digits before the decimal and exactly two after it; the value must
be 1–100,000 integer cents. A field ends at a semicolon, line ending, or end of
text. Spaces/tabs may separate words or trail the field. Source text is limited
to 8,000 characters. Other syntax goes to review; model confidence cannot waive
this grammar.

batches.message: docs(release-evidence): align serving identity and rollback walkthroughs [AI-03 AI-05]

replacements.new: Bring an immutable report, the dataset hash, a blocked broken-candidate run, the promotion/rollback transcript, and an explanation of what the small fixture suite does and does not establish. Include a successful `classifier.predict` response and a changed-prompt rejection. Explain how deployment restores matching code when a pointer rolls back.

**Does rollback change Bedrock automatically?** No. It changes the registry's active report. The supplied consumer blocks a mismatched loaded runtime; it does not deploy an old one. The regression test rolls the pointer back, observes the refusal, then loads the matching candidate and serves successfully.

**What if the model alias changes behind the same name?** Source/prompt/config hashes detect local changes, not an undisclosed provider change behind the same alias. Pin the most specific supported version, record configuration, and re-evaluate. Candidate identity is not a promise of deterministic model output.

**Senior follow-up:** extend the supplied identity-checking consumer into a versioned
runtime loader. Add per-category latency/cost, held-out datasets, repeated
stochastic runs and comparison with the current baseline. Do not silently load a
new configuration under an old passing report.

A passing report authorizes one candidate identity, not every future use of a model name.
The supplied consumer makes this boundary executable:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Active["Active report + revision"] --> Match{"Loaded candidate matches?"}
  Runtime["Source + prompt + model/config hashes"] --> Match
  Match -->|no| Block["Refuse; load matching runtime or evaluate anew"]
  Match -->|yes| Infer["Classify"]
  Infer --> Recheck{"Identity and revision unchanged?"}
  Recheck -->|yes| Reply["Return label + release + candidate ID"]
  Recheck -->|no| Conflict["Conflict; retry under current release"]
```

The check cannot recall a response already sent, hot-load an old runtime, or make a
provider's mutable alias immutable. Use a pinned provider version where available
and re-evaluate configuration changes.

6. **Promote deliberately.** Read the release revision. Only an eligible report can become active, and only if that revision still matches. Preserve the previous distinct release. Promoting the already-active report at the current revision is a no-op; a stale revision still conflicts.
7. **Serve only matching evidence.** `classifier.predict` resolves the active report and compares its candidate identity with the loaded runtime before inference. It checks candidate and release revision again before returning a label. Missing, ineligible or mismatched evidence blocks the response.
8. **Roll back explicitly.** Swap active and previous under the revision rule. If the loaded runtime differs from the old report, serving stays blocked until the matching code/configuration is loaded. The registry does not deploy code.

2. **Identify the candidate, not just the model.** `candidate.py` hashes the application source bytes, exact classification prompt, model identifier, inference configuration, retrieval version (`none-classifier-v1`) and gate policy. The report also records `AI_SOURCE_COMMIT` when supplied by the build. A missing commit is visible as null; the source-byte hash is still enforced. The dataset has its own hash.

| Repeat promotion | Active release-2, previous release-1; promote release-2 at revision 2 | No-op: preserve previous release-1 and revision 2 |
| Rollback | Active release-2, previous release-1, revision 2 | Active release-1, previous release-2, revision 3 |
| Changed prompt | Same model ID, different prompt after evaluation | `classifier.predict` refuses the unevaluated candidate |

batches.message: docs(ai-workbench): explain safe worker diagnostics and local/cloud evidence [AI-04 IN-03]

replacements.new:
Immediately querying may return `NOT_FOUND`; submission is not completion.
The worker emits one structured event per message with a hashed `message_ref`,
`category` and `retry` decision. It never logs source text, raw model output or
exception text. Correlate the hash with the restricted queue record when debugging.

| Category | Worker decision | Operator action |
|---|---|---|
| `ACCEPTED` / `REVIEW_REQUIRED` | Acknowledge the saved terminal outcome | Inspect the result; business review is not a retry |
| `provider_unavailable` / `processing_failure` | Fail that message for redelivery | Restore the dependency; inspect the saved result before retrying |
| `invalid_input` / `id_conflict` | Fail that message; bounded redrive to DLQ | Correct the producer or use a new versioned record ID; do not loop forever |

The queue visibility timeout is 1,080 seconds against a 180-second Lambda timeout.
The configured redrive policy bounds receives before moving failed work to the
DLQ. Invalid jobs are not silently acknowledged without a durable result. These
are supplied policies to exercise in your AWS account, not a claim of a live run.
| AWS fixture | Same deterministic responses | DynamoDB + S3, with SQS worker | After you deploy and execute the checks: evidence for your IAM, queue and storage integration |
